svg.title: Anatomy of a LiteX SoC
svg.desc: A typical LiteX SoC inside an FPGA. The bus masters at the top: the CPU (instruction and data buses), the DMAs of the cores (LiteEth, LitePCIe, LiteSDCard) and the host bridge (UARTBone, JTAGBone, Etherbone or PCIe) used by the host tools. They share the main bus, a Wishbone, AXI-Lite or AXI interconnect (shared bus or crossbar) generated by the SoC builder from the address map. Its slaves: the ROM holding the BIOS, the SRAM, the main RAM (LiteDRAM controller driving the DDR chips of the board) and the CSR bridge, which gives access to the CSR bus. On the CSR bus, every peripheral exposes its control/status registers (UART, timer, GPIO, SPI/I2C, LiteEth, LiteSDCard, LitePCIe, video, LiteScope...) and the EventManagers drive the interrupt lines back to the CPU. Outside the FPGA: the serial console and host bridge, the DDR, the Ethernet PHY, the SD card, the PCIe host.

g.font-family: Calibri, Carlito, 'Liberation Sans', Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif
g.text: LiteX SoC: generated from the target file, sys_clk domain
bus masters for the data transfers
the host tools read and write the whole bus (litex_server)
shared bus or crossbar, 32 to 512-bit, generated from the address map (SoCBusHandler), adapters between standards and widths
CSR bus: control/status registers of every core (AutoCSR), one bank per core, addresses in csr.h / csr.csv / csr.svd
